name: stand
note: master standing pose = rest drawing + pregnancy posture + hand library. Posture (research §3): lumbar extension (spineLower +4), upper trunk counter-leans back (spineUpper/chest -4 each), head/neck compensate to keep the gaze level and the ear over the feet (head x within 6 px of rest). Pelvis tilt is NOT a screen rotation in ¾ (it is about the hip axis), so it is suggested by tipping the bump (belly +3) instead of rotating the pelvis — keeps the feet planted. Clavicles level the shoulder line the chest rotation tilted. Arms hang plumb: upperArm -5.6 (anatomical) cancels the -4° trunk lean through the ¾ projection. R2: stronger counter-lean (spineUpper -6, chest -5; head/neck +7 keep the gaze level); far arm swings forward (-1) to clear the bump; far leg splayed 3° (wider pregnant base). R3: slight A-pose (shoulderAbd far -12 / near +6, asymmetric) opens negative space so the bump reads in silhouette; far leg splay -5. 11 Oct: far leg splay -1.5 (thighs overlap in ¾, no slot), far arm abduction -3 (hangs naturally; the far cardigan panel keeps the bump separate). R4: rig A-pose — far arm abduction -12, slight extension -4 and elbow 14 open a wedge of negative space so the bump's lower curve is on the solid silhouette (in ¾ the bump projects past a hanging far arm, so a plumb arm always hides it); near arm +9 opens the near armpit. R5: near arm +15 (armpit opens ≥0.1 H at the cuff).
